name: Modal verbs
note: Modals are followed by the bare infinitive. can/could ability & permission, must/have to obligation, mustn't prohibition vs don't have to = no obligation, should/ought to advice, might/may/could possibility. For deduction: must (sure it's true) / can't (sure it's false).

questions.q: You ______ get the 8.45 train. It doesn't stop at Yorkshire.
I'm learning Spanish because I want ______ speak when I'm in Mexico.
A: Look at the magician. He is sawing that woman in half! B: He ______ sawing her in half. It ______ a trick.
options: ought not to be / can be

questions.q: Shoes ______ be either black or brown.
In my country you ______ get married when you're sixteen.
To keep fit and stay healthy, you ______ enough of the right kinds of exercise.
I may ______ able to come to your party if I have the time.
questions.fs: I may be able to come to your party if I have the time.

questions.q: ______ we ______ have any vaccinations before we go to Barbados?
It is very difficult choice to ______ make.
______ you want some water?
questions.fs: Do you want some water?

questions.q: A retired person ______ go to work.
A: Did you enjoy the concert? B: It was OK, but I ______ to the theatre.
He probably ______ be back in time for dinner.
I love driving! ______ drive has changed my whole life.
If there is fuel shortage, solar energy ______ .
A: ______ . B: I'm sorry, but I haven't got my car.
options: Will you give me a lift?
Shall I drive you to school?
Could you drive a bit faster?

questions.q: I phoned yesterday, but I ______ get an answer. Where were you?
I wouldn't buy it unless I ______ it.
A: ______ . B: No, thank you. I've had enough.
Teenagers ______ study for exams.
If those two people ______ leave, the Whole firm would probably collapse.
A: I thought there was a cinema here. B: There ______ be. It's now a supermarket.
questions.x: used to = a past habit or state that is no longer true.

questions.q: You really ______ see that film because I know you'll like it.
questions.fs: You really should see that film because I know you'll like it.
questions.x: should = advice — the right thing to do. Followed by the bare infinitive (no 'to').

questions.q: You ______ for me; I could have found the way all right.
______ you able to understand the lesson this morning?
I know I ______ do it because I have done it before.
questions.fs: I know I can do it because I have done it before.

questions.q: I ______ to learn English fluently.
You ______ enter without a tie.
I went for a ten-mile run last Saturday. It nearly killed me! I ______ move on Sunday.
If we went to live in the tropics. I ______ buy some thin clothes.
I could ______ bought that car but I didn't have enough money to pay for the petrol.
questions.fs: I could have bought that car but I didn't have enough money to pay for the petrol.

questions.q: Speak up! I ______ hear you!
questions.x: can't = impossibility, or being sure it is not true. Followed by the bare infinitive (no 'to').

questions.q: ______ the pains come again, don't hesitate to phone me.
A: She can't sing. B: Neither ______ .
Children in my country ______ go to school when they're 7.
You'd better not try to bribe him. He ______ you to the police.
options: could report didn't have to go
might have reported didn't need to go
could have reported needn't have gone

questions.q: ______ open the windows. I'm cold.
I'd love ______ help you, but I can't. I'm sorry.
We can't wait any longer! Something ______ immediately.
They ______ do their homework today because it is a holiday at the school.
questions.fs: They don't have to do their homework today because it is a holiday at the school.

questions.q: When we got to the top of the mountain we ______ see for miles.
After looking at his notes again, he ______ to complete the exercise.
______ you pass the salt, please?
It's the right thing to do in this situation and it's my belief that you ______ to go.
questions.fs: It's the right thing to do in this situation and it's my belief that you ought to go.

questions.q: Let's go to the seminar. It ______ interesting.
We ______ leave now or we'll be late.
______ you speak French before you moved to Paris?
Children ______ taught to respect their elders.
I ______ like to listen to guitar music.
questions.x: would = an imagined / unreal situation, or politeness. Followed by the bare infinitive (no 'to').

questions.q: I phoned the plumber because I ______ smell gas in the kitchen.
A: The Chinese described flying machines. B: They ______ tremendous imaginations.
I ______ go to see the doctor last week because I was very ill.
questions.fs: I had to go to see the doctor last week because I was very ill.

questions.q: You should take an umbrella with you today, it ______ rain later.
questions.fs: You should take an umbrella with you today, it might rain later.

questions.q: I ______ to the doctor. I'm feeling much better.
I ______ speak French without a problem now because I have had many lessons.
questions.fs: I can speak French without a problem now because I have had many lessons.

questions.q: Nobody enjoys ______ get up at five o'clock in the morning.
Joan suggested that they ______ all go for a walk in the afternoon - provided it didn't keep on raining.
questions.x: should = advice — the right thing to do. Followed by the bare infinitive (no 'to').

questions.q: A: Were they playing tennis? B: No, they ______ .
Women ______ vote in England until 1922.
"You weren't supposed to do that." means: ______ .
options: You should do that, but you don't.
You should have done it, but you didn't.
You shouldn't do that, but you do.

questions.q: ______ you please bring me my notebook?
questions.fs: Will you please bring me my notebook?

questions.q: Pete: It ______ have been some time in 1947, I'm sure of that.
questions.fs: Pete: It must have been some time in 1947, I'm sure of that.
questions.x: must = obligation or strong necessity. Followed by the bare infinitive (no 'to').

questions.q: Lucy is very late. She ______ her train.
A: My car has been stolen. B: ______ .
______ you ______ find all the things you wanted at the shops?
If we don't book seats soon, we ______ to get into the concert.
______ you mind if I used your dictionary?
Every adult ______ go to work.
Powerful though they were, they never ______ to challenge the authority of the King.
You ______ do your homework. If you don't, you'll fail the examination.
Now there's no argument here. You ______ to finish on time because you have no choice.
questions.fs: Now there's no argument here. You have to finish on time because you have no choice.
questions.x: may = permission, or possibility. Followed by the bare infinitive (no 'to').

questions.q: It is very important to me, and I really ______ be late.
A: ______ I go? B: Yes, you can.
______ you really help me? If so, I should be most grateful.
questions.fs: Could you really help me? If so, I should be most grateful.

questions.q: A: He was driving on the right in Cyprus when he crashed. B: He ______ on the left.
Diner: I was thinking I ______ try the soup.
questions.fs: Diner: I was thinking I might try the soup.
questions.x: might = possibility (less sure than 'may'). Followed by the bare infinitive (no 'to').

questions.q: I ______ get into my house last night because I'd lost my key.
When I was a child my father ______ read me a story every night before bed.
Are you really suggesting that we ______ actually get into one of those ridiculous things?
questions.fs: Are you really suggesting that we should actually get into one of those ridiculous things?
questions.x: should = advice — the right thing to do. Followed by the bare infinitive (no 'to').

questions.q: It's quite clear that you ______ to visit their house, so why don't you?
questions.fs: It's quite clear that you want to visit their house, so why don't you?

questions.q: A: His brother won the marathon last year. B: He ______ very fast.
Mother is still in bed, and ______ my sister.
I say to myself each morning I really ______ write that letter.
questions.fs: I say to myself each morning I really must write that letter.
questions.x: must = obligation or strong necessity. Followed by the bare infinitive (no 'to').

questions.q: If you'd explained your problem to me, I ______ to help you.
I may ______ go to Paris next week because there is a very big exhibition there.
questions.fs: I may have to go to Paris next week because there is a very big exhibition there.

questions.q: The neighbors were having a row, and I ______ hear every word they said.
Your umbrella is wet. It ______ raining.
A: I bought this pen today and it doesn't work. B: ______ .
options: Could you fill it with ink?
Shall I give you another one?

questions.q: ______ I have your permission to leave the meeting early?
questions.fs: May I have your permission to leave the meeting early?
questions.x: will = a decision made now, a prediction, or a promise. Followed by the bare infinitive (no 'to').

questions.q: Since you have been working for hours, you ______ tired.
